hero.body:
A Fort Pierce man faces a manslaughter charge after a 34-year-old man died following a BB gun shooting on August 22 in the 2900 block of Avenue G. Jabari Cowart, 36, was arrested and taken to the St. Lucie County jail.

Fort Pierce Police officers responded to reports of a gunshot victim and found the 34-year-old male suffering from an injury. The victim was transported to Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died.

The initial investigation revealed that a group of males had been shooting a BB gun at trees when Cowart asked to use the BB gun. During the interaction, Cowart reportedly pointed the BB gun in the victim's direction and fired. Shortly thereafter, the victim collapsed.

The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation by Fort Pierce Police.

cards.body:
Fort Pierce is enforcing two-hour parking limits in parts of downtown, with citations now being issued to drivers who exceed the limit. Drivers who stay longer than two hours receive a $50 citation, which increases to $100 for repeat offenses. The initiative began in July and aims to increase parking turnover, improve traffic flow, and make it easier for visitors to find available spaces.

 Beryl Muise, owner of Notions Potions, said the two-hour parking limit has benefited her business. Muise said customers can now find parking spots and come into the store without getting frustrated driving around in circles. She said the spots would previously be full, making it difficult for customers with disabilities who cannot walk from the garage.

 The two-hour parking limits are enforced Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. One restaurant, which declined to comment on camera, said two hours is not long enough for their lunch rush, especially with limited parking in front of the establishment. Muise said weekends are less congested because offices like the public defender's office and title companies have employees present Monday through Friday but not on weekends.
cards.headline: Fort Pierce enforces two-hour parking limits downtown with $50 citations
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce now issues $50 citations to drivers who exceed two-hour parking limits in parts of downtown, with the penalty increasing to $100 for repeat offenses.

cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District responded to a residential fire Monday in the 400 block of East Erie Drive in Fort Pierce following reports of a residential structure fire. Fire district crews arrived at the scene and quickly attacked the fire, containing it to the area of origin.

 The containment prevented the fire from spreading to nearby mobile homes. The cause of the fire is being investigated by the Florida State Fire Marshals. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and the Fort Pierce Police Department also responded to the incident.
cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District contains residential fire on East Erie Drive in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District responded to a residential fire Monday in the 400 block of East Erie Drive in Fort Pierce, preventing it from spreading to nearby mobile homes.

cards.body:
Port St. Lucie residents cleaning up after Sunday evening's tornado said they received emergency alerts on their phones long after the storm had passed. Carol Cadotte, who lives near where the tornado started, said her phones went off 20 minutes after the tornado ripped parts of her roof off. Aaron Christiansen said he received the emergency alert after the storm had already hit his home.

 Cadotte said her house is old but made it through all the hurricanes without ever losing anything. The five-minute tornado peeled her roof off. She said in her nearly 30 years of living there, this was the first time she had major damage.

 Christiansen had about 10 seconds to react before the storm hit after he saw debris flying through his window. His patio furniture was submerged in his pool, his pool fence was blown toward his home, and debris was scattered across the ground. Christiansen, originally from Minnesota, said his experience with tornado-like weather helped him know what precautions to take.
cards.headline: Port St. Lucie residents receive tornado emergency alert 20 minutes after storm passed
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie residents cleaning up tornado damage Monday expressed frustration with emergency alerts arriving well after the tornado had already hit their homes.

cards.body:
Marlene Torres was celebrating her birthday in Jensen Beach Sunday night before returning home to find the storm had moved through her Port St. Lucie neighborhood. Her birthday fell on Monday, August 24, which is also the anniversary of Hurricane Andrew. Her home was not damaged, but she needed an electrician to fix her meter.

 Torres was living in Miami when Hurricane Andrew hit the region. She said the tornado cannot be compared to Andrew, which was life-altering for the longest time with repairs taking months and months. Torres said she is thankful not to have to go through that again.

 Mitch Brewer had debris piled out front, most of it from a shed he had tied down. Brewer said it looks like the shed caught some heavy updrafts and left. He said he had been thinking about demolishing the old shed at some point, but the storm beat him to it.

 Brewer said living in the mid-South made him familiar with tornadoes. Florida sees about 65 to 70 tornadoes a year and has a higher frequency per 10,000 square miles than any other state, including Oklahoma.
cards.headline: Tornado moves through Port St. Lucie neighborhood on Hurricane Andrew anniversary
cards.teaser: Marlene Torres returned home Sunday night from celebrating her birthday in Jensen Beach to find the tornado had moved through her Port St. Lucie neighborhood, on the same date as the Hurricane Andrew anniversary.

hero.body:
An EF0 tornado touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening, damaging 20 to 30 homes along a 2.1-mile path with winds between 65 and 75 mph. The National Weather Service confirmed the tornado began at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club, before moving over the St. Lucie River and returning to land in the Bay St. Lucie community.

 Will Ulrich, warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service Melbourne office, announced the findings Monday morning during a press conference at Jessica Clinton Park. The tornado, classified as a landspout, moved over the St. Lucie River where it became a waterspout for five to seven minutes before returning onshore around 6:20 p.m. The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, causing numerous downed trees and large branches along with damage to tile-roofed homes.

 The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, causing downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. The entire event lasted 14 to 15 minutes. Damage included roof damage, soffit damage, and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations, with approximately 20 to 30 percent of roof covers removed from some homes.

 No injuries were reported from the tornado. Residents spent Monday cleaning up debris from pools, yards, and damaged structures. Aaron Christiansen pulled patio furniture from his submerged pool after his patio broke apart during the storm, while Janelle Pierre-Louis reported her front door caved in with dirt coming through cracks. The National Weather Service worked with Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct the damage survey.

He said he had been thinking about demolishing the old shed at some point, but the storm beat him to it. Brewer said living in the mid-South made him familiar with tornadoes. Florida sees about 65 to 70 tornadoes a year and has a higher frequency per 10,000 square miles than any other state, including Oklahoma.
cards.headline: Tornado moves through Port St. Lucie neighborhood on Hurricane Andrew anniversary
cards.teaser: Marlene Torres returned home Sunday night from celebrating her birthday in Jensen Beach to find the tornado had moved through her Port St. Lucie neighborhood, on the same date as the Hurricane Andrew anniversary.

cards.body:
Will Ulrich of the National Weather Service said the Port St. Lucie tornado was unique because it formed as a landspout rather than spinning out of a rotating supercell thunderstorm. Landspouts form closer to the surface along the leading edge of thunderstorm updrafts. The circulations are not particularly strong, making them difficult to see on radar before they form.

Ulrich said it was not raining when the tornado touched down, with heavy rain arriving only after it passed through. This is typical of how landspouts form. Ulrich explained the more heat present, the more vigorous boundary collisions become, and it has been abnormally warm lately.

The tornado was unusually long for this type, lasting 14 to 15 minutes. While landspouts are more common during summer months in Florida, any one location experiencing a tornado remains historically rare. The National Weather Service worked with Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct interviews with residents and piece together the timeline of the event.
cards.headline: National Weather Service explains landspout formation after Port St. Lucie tornado
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie tornado formed as a landspout along the leading edge of a thunderstorm updraft, making it difficult to detect on radar before it touched down Sunday evening.

An EF0 tornado touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening, damaging 20 to 30 homes along a 2.1-mile path with winds between 65 and 75 mph. The National Weather Service confirmed the tornado began at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club, before moving over the St. Lucie River and returning to land in the Bay St. Lucie community.

Will Ulrich, warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service Melbourne office, announced the findings Monday morning during a press conference at Jessica Clinton Park. The tornado, classified as a landspout, moved over the St. Lucie River where it became a waterspout for five to seven minutes before returning onshore around 6:20 p.m. The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, causing numerous downed trees and large branches along with damage to tile-roofed homes.

The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, causing downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. The entire event lasted 14 to 15 minutes. Damage included roof damage, soffit damage, and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations, with approximately 20 to 30 percent of roof covers removed from some homes.

No injuries were reported from the tornado. Residents spent Monday cleaning up debris from pools, yards, and damaged structures. Aaron Christiansen pulled patio furniture from his submerged pool after his patio broke apart during the storm, while Janelle Pierre-Louis reported her front door caved in with dirt coming through cracks. The National Weather Service worked with Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct the damage survey.

cards.body:
Fort Pierce is issuing $50 citations to drivers who exceed two-hour parking limits in parts of downtown, with repeat offenses rising to $100. The enforcement, which began in July, aims to increase parking turnover, improve traffic flow, and make it easier for visitors to find available spaces, according to city officials. The limits are enforced Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m.

Beryl Muise, owner of Notions Potions, said the two-hour limit has benefited her business. "I have seen my customers be able to find a parking spot and come into the store, and then get back into their car and be able to leave. They didn't get frustrated driving around in circles looking for a spot," she said. Muise said the limits help customers with disabilities who cannot walk from the two free parking garages nearby.

One restaurant, which declined to comment on camera, said two hours is not long enough for their lunch rush, especially with limited parking in front of the establishment. Muise acknowledged the parking limit may not work for all businesses but said weekends are less congested because office employees are not present. "On the weekends, it's better for the retail and the restaurants. You don't have as many offices that are here, you know? Like the public defender's office," she said.
cards.headline: Fort Pierce issues $50 citations under new two-hour downtown parking limit
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce is now issuing citations to drivers who exceed two-hour parking limits in parts of downtown. The enforcement, which began in July, is drawing mixed reactions from local businesses.

cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District responded to a residential structure fire in the 400 block of East Erie Drive in Fort Pierce on Monday and contained the blaze before it could spread to nearby mobile homes. Fire district crews quickly attacked the fire upon arrival, containing it to the area of origin. The Florida State Fire Marshal is investigating the cause of the fire.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and the Fort Pierce Police Department also responded to the incident.
cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District contains Fort Pierce residential fire, prevents spread to mobile homes
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District contained a residential structure fire on East Erie Drive in Fort Pierce on Monday, preventing it from spreading to nearby mobile homes. The cause remains under investigation by the Florida State Fire Marshal.

cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man is facing a manslaughter charge after a 34-year-old man died following a BB gun shooting on August 22, 2026. Jabari Cowart, 36, was charged with manslaughter and taken to the St. Lucie County Jail after the incident in the 2900 block of Avenue G.

Fort Pierce Police officers responded to reports of a gunshot victim and found the 34-year-old male suffering from an injury. The victim was transported to Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died.

The initial investigation revealed that a group of males had been shooting a BB gun at trees when Cowart asked to use the BB gun. During the interaction, Cowart reportedly pointed the BB gun in the victim's direction and fired. Shortly thereafter, the victim collapsed. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation.
cards.headline: Fort Pierce man charged with manslaughter after BB gun shooting kills 34-year-old
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce man is facing a manslaughter charge after a 34-year-old man died following a BB gun shooting on August 22. Jabari Cowart, 36, allegedly pointed the BB gun at the victim and fired during a group outing.
